clue.text: Queen of Hearts in unreal PGA final

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters

explanation.surface: A card-game queen turns up at an imaginary golf championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen of Hearts' reads as one card, but the clue splits after 'Queen': 'Hearts' tells you to take the middles of the next three words, and each gives a different number of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Regina is Latin for queen, seen in a monarch's signature as the R of ER.

clue.text: Ten hours lost below the equator

indicators.note: letters that are lost have gone astray from their order

explanation.surface: A traveller crossing into the southern hemisphere loses ten hours to jet lag.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like time-zone arithmetic; 'lost' is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain geographical sense: the equator divides the globe, and whatever lies beneath it on the map is in the south.

clue.text: Kind of star to reject amateur lines

parts.note: to bin is to throw out

explanation.surface: A star performer turns down the amateurs' script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity snubbing amateurs; here it is astronomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A binary star is a pair of stars orbiting each other.

clue.text: Comply with Klingon on the telephone

indicators.note: a phone carries only sound, so the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: the alien race's name, said out, is a two-word phrase meaning to hold fast

explanation.surface: Someone takes orders over the phone from a Star Trek alien.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound gives a phrase, not the answer's letters: 'cling on' must then be turned into its synonym STICK TO. Klingons are the warrior aliens of Star Trek.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the figurative sense: holding fast to a plan or rule means obeying it.

clue.text: Offensive posters from Tesla introducing luxury car

indicators.note: the letter that introduces a word is its first

explanation.surface: Rude billboards from Tesla announce a new top-of-the-range model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posters' looks like billboards; here it means people who post online.
explanation.definitionFit: Trolls post deliberately offensive messages online.

clue.text: 8 stone
Plane's carrying company of 8 biblical authors

indicators.note: one thing carrying another holds it inside

parts.note: plane = jet, plus the S of the possessive
Hovis is a British bread company; 8 across is BREAD

explanation.surface: An aircraft is loaded with a bread firm's staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jehovists are the scholars' name for the source of the Pentateuch that calls God Yahweh (Jehovah).
explanation.definitionFit: Jehovists are the supposed writers of the Yahwist strand of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Walter White finishes Breaking Bad making money

indicators.note: a word's finish is its last letter
one word breaking another splits it open to sit inside

parts.note: last letters of WalteR and WhitE

explanation.surface: Walter White, the chemistry teacher of the TV drama Breaking Bad, finishes the show rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic title is a trap: it must be pulled apart so that its first word becomes an instruction acting on its second.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang sense: 1960s American slang for cash, fitting a drug-dealing hero who made a fortune.

clue.text: Terrible miscue at the end from Allan Lamb's partner?

indicators.note: a terrible shot is all over the place
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A cricketer's batting partner plays a dreadful shot at the end of the innings.
explanation.walkthrough: Allan Lamb was an England batsman, so 'partner' and 'miscue' look like cricket; the question mark flags lamb the meat, and mint sauce is the traditional British sauce served with roast lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint sauce is served alongside roast lamb.

clue.text: Student tucked into square meal

indicators.note: something tucked into another sits inside it

parts.note: four is a square number, two squared

explanation.surface: A student tucks into a proper hearty meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square meal' reads as one phrase and 'tucked into' as eating; the words split, with 'square' giving FOUR. Meal here is ground grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Meal is coarsely ground grain, and flour is finely ground meal.

clue.text: Food served up in Emirati Palace

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from the bottom
the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A meal is brought out at a palace in the Emirates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served' sounds like waiters; with 'up' it means read the hidden letters bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the Middle Eastern flatbread is one kind of food, and fits the bread theme.

clue.text: Shop window broken by king and queen

indicators.note: something broken by another has that other sitting inside the gap

explanation.surface: Royals smash a shop window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop window' reads as one thing, but 'Shop' stands alone as the definition and 'window' is a particular kind that juts out from a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the baker's premises are one kind of shop, here the one selling 8 across.

clue.text: Suspect ending in Silent Witness reveals matching threads

indicators.note: a suspect account is not to be trusted as it stands
the ending is the last letter

explanation.surface: A suspect in the last episode of the TV drama Silent Witness is exposed by fibres on clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic title is split: only the last letter of 'Silent' is used, with 'Witness' taken whole. Silent Witness is a British forensic crime drama, so 'threads' look like evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinset is a matching cardigan and jumper, and threads is slang for clothes.

clue.text: Old lady wasting money in Virgin store

indicators.note: to waste something is to lose it, so the M goes

parts.note: MARY, the Virgin, without M for money

explanation.surface: A grandmother blows her savings in a Virgin Megastore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin store' reads as the Branson chain; 'store' is the definition. Granary is also a brand of malted bread, in the 8 across theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a building for keeping threshed grain is one kind of store.

clue.text: City great arranged police protection

indicators.note: arranged letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A big city sets up a police guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City great' reads as praise for a city; 'great' is fodder and 'arranged' shuffles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Riot gear is the helmets and shields that protect police at disturbances.

clue.text: Filling of hot Caribbean sandwich

indicators.note: the filling is what lies inside, the middle letters

parts.note: hot in the sexy sense is a six-letter word; drop its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A spicy filling goes into a Caribbean sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' must first become EROTIC before its filling is taken; the sandwich picture makes it look like chilli.
explanation.definitionFit: A roti is a flatbread wrapped round a curry filling, a Caribbean staple.

clue.text: Every year, Wimbledon champion makes a fuss

parts.note: Rod Laver, Wimbledon winner in the 1960s

explanation.surface: A tennis great kicks up a stink every summer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin 'per annum' shrinks to PA, and the champion is Rod Laver, the Australian who won Wimbledon four times.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word began as a West African trading parley and came to mean tiresome, long-winded bother.

clue.text: Austin Powers finally in pieces

parts.note: the Austin Allegro, a 1970s British car

indicators.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: The film spy Austin Powers ends up in bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Austin Powers' reads as the film character; split it, and Austin is the carmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegro is a brisk piece or movement of music.

clue.text: Drink of Manhattan stirs up American Dad

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from the bottom

explanation.surface: A cocktail gets the father from the cartoon American Dad worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic title is split, as 'stirs up' and 'American Dad' look fused. 'Of Manhattan' marks the definition as American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda pop is the American name for a fizzy soft drink.

clue.text: Wind octet entertaining men with new instrument

indicators.note: to wind is to twist, rearranging the letters
one thing entertaining another holds it inside

explanation.surface: A wind octet puts on a show for players with a new instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind octet' reads as a band of woodwind players; 'Wind' is the anagram instruction, and 'men with new' are what the shuffled octet holds. A cornetto is also a British ice-cream cone, not meant here.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornetto is a Renaissance wooden wind instrument played with a cup mouthpiece.

clue.text: Writer is almost drained by conclusion of Jonathan Swift

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so the last letter goes
the conclusion is the last letter

parts.note: the writer is = I am, I'M

explanation.surface: An author is worn out by the ending of a Jonathan Swift book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jonathan Swift' is split: Swift is the definition. The setter referring to himself as 'writer' gives I'M; 'by' puts N beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift and nimble both mean quick in movement.

clue.text: American 8 lying about in Balmoral Lodge

indicators.note: lying the other way round reads backwards
the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An American guest lounges around the royal estate at Balmoral.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 across is BREAD, slang for money, so 'American 8' is American money. Balmoral is the royal family's Scottish castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The dollar is American currency, and bread is money.

clue.text: Country scrapping nuclear limit

indicators.note: scrapping something throws it away

parts.note: N = nuclear, the letter to be thrown out

explanation.surface: A nation abandons its nuclear programme and sets a cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuclear limit' reads as a treaty cap, but 'limit' is the definition and verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To demark is to mark out the limits of something.

clue.text: No longer hooked on holidays we hear

indicators.note: the word is heard, not read

explanation.surface: Someone kicks an addiction while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooked on' looks like addiction; it is an anchor hooked on the seabed. An anchor is aweigh once lifted clear.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor aweigh has just come free of the bottom.

clue.text: A Trump supporter going round The Lizard

indicators.note: turning round reverses the direction

explanation.surface: A Trump fan tours the Lizard peninsula in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lizard is Cornwall's southern tip, so the capital L makes it a place; here it is the reptile. The whole of A MAGA turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an Old World genus of reptile, so 'The Lizard' names a whole group of which this is one.

clue.text: Rolling Stone possibly cutting hair to become object of attraction

indicators.note: something cutting another goes into it

parts.note: barnet is British rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair)
Rolling Stone is a magazine, MAG

explanation.surface: A Rolling Stones guitarist gets a haircut and becomes a heart-throb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stone' suggests the band; 'possibly' marks it as an example of a mag.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal reading of an idiom: 'object of attraction' usually means a loved one, but a straight iron magnet physically attracts.

clue.text: Spooner's mistress delivers paper

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: mistress = LADY, as in lady of the house; swap its two syllables' opening sounds

explanation.surface: A kept woman does the paper round.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap happens inside one word: LADY's two syllables trade their first sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a newspaper published every day.

clue.text: Son with money belonging to us is 8

explanation.surface: A son with the family money is in the bread business.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 across is BREAD, and DOUGH is another word for both money and bread's raw form.
explanation.definitionFit: Sourdough is bread leavened with a fermented starter.
